answer: To change the currency for your course (or any paid transactions on your site), go to Language & Region in your site's dashboard (or Settings > Language & Region), click the Currency drop-down menu, select the relevant currency, and click Save. Important: Your site's currency must match the currency in your payment provider account to accept payments, and if you have a multilingual site, the currency you select will apply to all language versions.

To see what items customers added to their cart, go to Reports in your site's dashboard and view the Stores section. Use the abandoned cart reports: Most Abandoned Products (shows products placed in cart but not bought), Abandoned Carts Funnel (shows how many carts were abandoned vs. recovered), and Abandoned Carts Summary (detailed view filterable by customer type, product value, etc.). To see how items were sold, use the Sales by Product Variant or Sales by Product Category reports in the Stores section, or go to All Reports and view the Sales section to use the Sales by item report, which gives a breakdown of specific items and services sold.

If you're encountering a region or currency error with Wix Payments, first verify that Wix Payments is available in your country. It is currently only available in: Austria (EUR), Belgium (EUR), Brazil (BRL), Canada (CAD), Finland (EUR), Germany (EUR), Ireland (EUR), Italy (EUR), Lithuania (EUR), Netherlands (EUR), Portugal (EUR), Spain (EUR), Switzerland (CHF), United Kingdom (GBP), and United States (USD). If your region is not listed, Wix Payments will not be available and you will see locally available payment providers instead. Additionally, ensure the currency set in your Wix site matches the currency in your Wix Payments account. To change your site currency, go to Settings > Language & Region in your dashboard, select your currency from the drop-down menu, and click Save. Also check your business location at the top right of the Accept Payments page in your dashboard to ensure it is correct, as this affects which payment options are available to you.

Since the logo appears on your live site but not in the editor, first check your site history to locate the last saved version containing the logo and restore it if it was saved over. Make sure you are viewing the correct page in the editor that corresponds to the live page. The logo may be placed outside the site's gridlines; hold Ctrl (Cmd on Mac) + Shift and press M to toggle through page elements until you locate it. If still unresolved, follow the steps in the Wix Technical Assistant.

Since your site is published and not password protected, try these steps from the Wix documentation: 1) Check that search engines can index your site by going to your SEO Dashboard > Go to SEO Settings under Tools and settings and ensure the 'Let search engines index your site' toggle is enabled. 2) Check if your specific pages have a 'noindex' robots meta tag or are set to prevent search engines from indexing them in the Editor. 3) Check if your pages have any 301 redirects in the URL Redirect Manager and delete them if they are preventing indexing. 4) Reset your page's canonical tag to default in the Advanced SEO tab if you've customized it. 5) Ensure your pages contain at least 250-400 words of content, as pages with insufficient content may return soft 404 or 'no index' errors. 6) Add internal links to other pages on your site to help search engines understand page relationships. 7) Use the Wix SEO Setup Checklist to optimize your site and submit it directly to Google for indexing. 8) Check the index status of your page using Google's URL Inspection tool or the Wix Site Inspection tool. 9) Check Google Search Console for any manual actions applied to your page. Note that it can take time for Google to crawl and index changes, and search engines cannot guarantee every page will be indexed.

To reassign your domain to a different site in your Wix account: 1) Go to Domains in your Wix account. 2) Scroll to the domain you want to reassign. 3) Click the Domain Actions icon (or More Actions icon) on the right and select 'Assign to a Different Site'. 4) Select the site you want to connect the domain to and click Next. 5) If that site is currently connected to a different domain, choose either 'Redirect it to the primary domain' (to redirect your domain to the site's existing primary domain) or 'Replace the current primary domain' (to connect your domain and disconnect the site's current domain). 6) Click Assign. Note: The site must have an active Premium or Studio plan for the domain to be assigned to it.

To connect Google Analytics 4 (GA4) to your Wix site: 1) Create a GA4 property in your Google Analytics account using the GA4 Setup Assistant, then copy your measurement ID (found under Web stream details). 2) In your Wix site's dashboard, go to Marketing Integrations, click View under Google Analytics, then click the Show More icon in the top right corner and select Edit. 3) Paste your GA4 measurement ID in the pop-up (ensure no extra spaces before the code). 4) Optionally select the IP Anonymization checkbox to hide visitor IP addresses from Google. 5) Click Save. Note: Universal Analytics properties stopped collecting data on July 1, 2023, so upgrading to GA4 is recommended.

The message "Your subscription has been suspended by your reseller" means your Google Workspace business email purchased through Wix has either expired or has a payment issue. To reactivate it: 1) Go to the Business Email page in your Wix account to check the status. 2) If the subscription has expired, click Renew Subscription. 3) If it is still active but payment failed, go to Payment Methods (or the Premium Subscriptions section), click Actions > Update > Next, update your card details, and click Update. If your renewal payment was declined (e.g., expired card, insufficient funds, or not approved for recurring payments), contact your bank to resolve it. If the subscription was already canceled, you must repurchase the business email. Note: If you did not accept the Google Product Agreement and Terms of Service in your business email admin account, the email will also be suspended—in that case, contact Wix Customer Care.

There are several common reasons a 50% off coupon may not apply. Check the following: 1) Promo code link visibility - ensure the 'Enter a promo code' link is enabled on the Cart Page and the font color contrasts with the background (go to Pages & Menu > Store Pages > Cart Page > Settings > Settings tab > select Promo code link checkbox, then Design tab > Links color box). 2) Coupon validity dates - verify the coupon hasn't expired; edit start/end dates in Coupons in your dashboard if needed. 3) Coupon activation - ensure the coupon is activated (go to Coupons, select Not active from Status dropdown if needed, click More Actions > Activate). 4) Usage limits - check if the total usage limit or one-use-per-person limit was reached; remove limitations or edit the number of uses in the coupon settings. 5) Code entry - ensure no extra blank spaces were added; have the customer copy and paste the code exactly. Coupons are not case-sensitive.

To adjust the menu layout on your mobile site, click the menu icon in your mobile editor, then click Edit Menu. For the menu container layout, click the menu container and then the Layout icon to choose alignment: Full Screen (opens to full screen), Left (opens to the left of the screen), or Right (opens to the right of the screen). For menu items layout, click the mobile menu and then the Layout icon to set how text is aligned (left, right, or center of the menu container) and how the submenu arrow is aligned (left or right of the item text).

To customize the layout of products in a Grid Gallery, go to the page in the editor containing the gallery, click the gallery, and then click the Settings icon. Click the Layout tab and customize the available options: General (toggle to stretch the gallery across the browser and set margin size), Product grid (choose Fixed or Responsive grid behavior—Responsive adjusts rows and columns to screen size but only works when stretched to full width), Product images (select how images are displayed), Add to Cart button (choose placement), Product info (choose a product card layout option), Product options (toggle to display only color options or limit color options), and Ribbons (select where the ribbon appears and adjust padding).

To troubleshoot a site unable to provide a secure connection (SSL/HTTPS issues), follow these steps: 1) Verify your DNS records are correct based on your connection method—if connected via name servers, ensure your domain host has the correct Wix name servers and your Wix account has default A and CNAME records; if connected via pointing, ensure your domain host has A record pointing to 185.230.63.107 and CNAME pointing to pointing.wixdns.net; if purchased from Wix, check default A and CNAME records in your Wix account. 2) Wait up to 48 hours for domain propagation if you recently updated DNS records. 3) If your domain was purchased outside Wix, ensure DNSSEC is not signed. 4) Check any HTML elements on your site to ensure they contain only HTTPS code (not HTTP). 5) Note that older operating systems may fail to recognize modern SSL certificates—update your OS if needed. If issues persist after these steps, submit a ticket with Wix Customer Care.

If your automated emails triggered by form submissions are not sending, follow these troubleshooting steps: 1) Check automation statistics in your dashboard (Automations > hover over automation > More Actions > View email stats) to confirm if the email was sent. 2) Check the recipient's spam folder and whitelist: no-reply@test.wixshoutout.com, @automations.ascendbywix.com (if no confirmed reply-to email set), or your confirmed reply-to email address. 3) Verify the recipient's email address is active and subscribed (look for 'SUBSCRIBED' label on their contact card) - emails won't send to inactive contacts. 4) Verify the recipient's email address is valid. 5) For Wix Forms specifically: confirm the form was successfully submitted (check submissions table), ensure the correct form is selected in your trigger settings, verify the form includes an email field with the correct field type (Email Field), ensure the email field is synced to your Contact List as 'Email' or 'Email (Main)', and check if the contact has multiple email addresses (automated emails may go to an additional email rather than the primary one). Also ensure you are logged out when testing, as logged-in submissions merge email addresses under one contact.

According to the Google Ads with Wix refund policy, ad credits added to Google Ads with Wix are paid with a monthly subscription or a one-time payment, and these payments are non-refundable. If you pause a campaign, your remaining ad credits remain in your account and you can resume the campaign using those remaining credits at any time.

The Right Click Protect app is available from the Wix App Market and helps protect your site content by displaying a copyright message when visitors right-click on your content. When a visitor right-clicks, they'll see a message informing them that the content is copyrighted. You can customize this message through the app's settings. To add it: Go to your editor, click Add Apps (or App Market) on the left side, search for 'Right Click Protect' in the search bar, click 'Add to Site', and optionally click Settings to edit the displayed message. Important limitation: The app does not prevent visitors from using Ctrl+C to copy your content.

Collection limits depend on your account type and plan. For free sites in the Wix Studio platform, the limit is 10,000 total collection items. For free sites not in Wix Studio (or if you leave Wix Studio), the limit is 1,000 collection items. If you upgrade to a Premium or Studio plan, your quota changes to the limit included in that plan (for example, a plan with 500,000 items). Additionally, you can store up to 500KB of data in a single item's total collection fields (this limit does not apply to image, document, multi document, video, audio, or media gallery fields). Note: Wix Stores has separate product limits of up to 50,000 products, 6 product options per product, 100 choices per option, and 1,000 variants per product.

If you're receiving payments using the manual (offline) method, you must mark them as paid before they appear in your payments page. Go to Payments in your site's dashboard, find the relevant transaction, and mark it as paid so it will then show up in your payment history.

To update the og:image for your entire site, open your site's settings, click Website settings, scroll down to General social image and click Upload Image, select an image or click + Upload Media to upload a new one, click Choose File to add it, click Save at the top of the dashboard, and publish your site. To reinstall Wix Blog, first delete it and then re-add it. To delete: In the Wix Editor, click Pages & Menu on the left, hover Blog Pages, click the Settings icon, then click Delete Blog and confirm. In the Studio Editor, click the Pages icon, scroll to Blog Pages, hover and click the More actions icon, then Delete Blog and confirm. To re-add: In the editor, click the Add Elements icon, click Blog, then Add to Site (or go to the Wix App Market, search 'Wix Blog', and click Add to Site). Note: Deleting Wix Blog does not permanently delete your content—re-adding it restores your content but does not restore your settings or additional blog elements like Post List. If loading issues persist after reinstalling, the documentation recommends first trying to open your blog in an Incognito window and clearing your browser cache and cookies.

To add more menu titles to your site header, you can add new menu items through the Pages & Menu panel or by managing an advanced menu. In the Wix Editor, click Pages & Menu on the left side, then click Add Menu Item at the bottom of the panel. You can add a Dropdown (non-clickable title) to organize items beneath it, or add pages, links, or sections. If you are using an advanced menu, click the menu in your editor, click Manage Menu, then click + Add Menu Item and select Dropdown title to add a new title, then drag and drop items under it.

To customize the text in automated client emails (confirmation, cancellation, reminders) in Wix Bookings: Go to Booking Settings in your site's dashboard, click Emails & SMS notifications, hover over the automation you want to customize and click Edit. For reminder emails you can also click Edit next to Timing to adjust when they send. Scroll down to Action 1 and choose what to customize: under Manage details you can edit the sender's name and reply-to email; under Create an email you can optionally switch the template (note this replaces existing changes), then click Edit to customize existing elements, add more elements, include an ICS calendar attachment (confirmation/cancellation only), set the email type, and select recipients. You can also add dynamic values (variables) to the subject line, preview text, or email content by clicking + Dynamic Value / + Add Dynamic Value and selecting from the drop-down, with optional fallback text. Click Save to confirm your changes.

To customize your Wix Store Product Page, go to your Editor, click Pages & Menu > Store Pages > Product Page, then click the Product Page element. 

**Layout & Image Display:** Click the Layout tab to select a layout. Enable 'Stretch to full width' if desired. Under 'Show thumbnails', choose how thumbnails display. Set the 'Image ratio' and select how images are resized (Crop to same size or Fit to maintain aspect ratio). Enable 'Zoom on image' if available for your layout. Use 'Reset to original layout' to revert changes.

**Button Text:** Click the Text tab to edit button text. You can customize: Add to Cart (main purchase button), Buy Now, Subscribe Now (for subscriptions), Out of Stock (automatic when inventory is zero), and Back in Stock/Notify When Available (if back-in-stock notifications are enabled). Note: If you disabled the Add to Cart or Buy Now buttons in the Settings tab, those text options won't appear.

**Additional Settings:** In the Settings tab, you can show/hide elements like the Add to Cart button, Buy Now button, wishlist icon, and social share icons, and choose where customers are directed when clicking Add to Cart (success pop-up, side cart, cart page, or stay on page). In the Design tab, customize colors, fonts, button styles, backgrounds, and product details alignment.

To access the Google Maps element in your footer, first try the Layers panel: click the Layers icon at the bottom of your editor, click Footer, then find and click the Google Maps element in the list to select it. If the map is hidden behind another element, use the Overlapping Items feature: right-click the element covering the map, hover over 'Overlapping Items', and select the Google Maps element from the list. If you still cannot select it, check that your footer is not frozen: click the footer, click the Settings icon, and disable the Freeze Footer toggle. You can also hold Ctrl (Cmd on Mac) + Shift and press M to toggle through elements until you reach the map. Once selected, you can remove the element.

To add new bank details to Wix Payments: Go to Accept Payments in your site's dashboard, click Manage next to Wix Payments, then click Edit Account Details (next to Account Details). Enter the new bank details under Bank Details, then click Save and Resubmit. Important: Whenever you make a change, Wix must verify your information, which can take up to 7 business days. During this time your account status returns to Accepting Payments, meaning you can accept payments but cannot receive payouts until verification is complete.

To customize the My Wishlist page (where customers view their saved items), go to your editor and navigate to the Members Area: In the Wix Editor, click Pages & Menu on the left, click Members Area, then click the My Wishlist page, select it in the Editor, click Settings, and customize using the available options. In Editor X, click Pages at the top, click Members Page, click the Member Menu, then Manage and Navigate, select My Wishlist, click the page in the Editor, click Settings, and customize. You can optionally add an 'Add to Cart' button to the wishlist page to make purchasing easier for customers.

Your payments go to your bank account via payouts. After a customer pays, the funds go through processing (usually 2-5 business days), then are added to a scheduled payout (daily, weekly, or monthly depending on your settings), and finally sent to your bank account where they typically arrive within 3-5 business days. You can view all previous and upcoming payouts, including which payments are included in each one, by going to Payouts in your site's dashboard. Note that payouts require your Wix Payments account to be verified and Active, and there must be an available balance of at least $1.

A DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN error means your domain's DNS records are not resolving. Since you haven't changed anything, start by checking these items in order: 1) Make sure your site is published (click Publish at the top right of your editor, then Done). 2) Check that your Premium or Studio plan subscription is still Active in Premium Subscriptions/My Premium plans — if Expired, upgrade to reconnect. 3) Check that your domain is assigned to the correct site in Domains (click Assign next to 'Not Assigned to a Site', or use Assign to a Different Site). 4) Check your domain's status and expiry date at whois.com — the domain must have an active status; if expired or in redemption, resolve payment/renewal with your registrar. 5) Verify your DNS records are correct. If your domain was purchased from Wix, go to Domains > Domain Actions > Manage DNS Records and confirm A record: 185.230.63.107 and CNAME record: initial.wixdns.net. If connected via pointing, log in to your domain host account and confirm A Record Host @ (or blank) Points to 185.230.63.107 and CNAME Host www Points to pointing.wixdns.net. Note: since January 17, 2024 some legacy DNS records are no longer supported for pointing connections — update to the records above if needed. 6) If you recently changed any DNS records or name servers, wait up to 48 hours for propagation. If issues persist after these checks, contact Wix Customer Care.

Since you are receiving form submissions but the automation is not triggering, check the following based on Wix Automations troubleshooting: 1) Verify the correct form is selected in your trigger settings - if you set a specific form rather than 'Any', ensure the right form is chosen. 2) Check your trigger filters and configuration in the automation editor to ensure the form submission passes the filter. 3) Check if 'Trigger once per person' is enabled, which limits the automation to run only once per contact. 4) Check for any delay configured between the trigger and action. 5) For New Wix Forms specifically: ensure your form includes an email field (required for 'Send an email' actions) or email/phone field (for other actions), that the email field is the correct field type, and that it is synced to 'Email' or 'Email (Main)' in your Contact List. 6) Check automation statistics in your dashboard to see trigger counts. 7) If testing while logged in, note that your test submissions may merge with your logged-in contact, affecting delivery. If the issue persists after these checks, contact Wix support with a screenshot or video.

To find the Address section in a room: Go to your site's dashboard, click the Hotels tab on the left, then click the Rooms tab. Click the Edit icon for an existing room type (or Create New to add a new one), then scroll down to the Address section. Click the 'Show map location' toggle to enable the address option, then enter the city, state, country, street address, and zip code, and click Save. Important: You can only add an address to a room after you've set up your hotel. If you're adding your first room and can't find the address section, add the room without the address first, then come back to add the address after setting up your hotel.

To resize your gallery in the desktop Wix Editor, click the gallery, then click and drag the stretch handles on the gallery's edges to make it bigger or smaller. If you're unable to resize using the stretch handles, the gallery is likely set to full width—you can disable this by clicking the Stretch icon and toggling off 'Stretch to full width'. Alternatively, you can stretch the gallery to full width by clicking the Stretch icon and enabling the 'Stretch to full width' toggle, then optionally adjust the Margins slider (limit: 80 pixels).

To update the terms & conditions checkbox at checkout in Wix Stores: Go to Checkout settings in your site's dashboard. Click Policies. Select the checkbox next to the policy you want to display and enter the policy text. To make customers agree to the policy before completing checkout, click the Policy agreement checkbox toggle to enable it. Optionally, select the Checked by default checkbox if you want the agreement checked by default.

Wix offers a 14-day money-back guarantee for new Premium plans (including Premium Light). If you purchased your plan within the last 14 days, you are eligible for a full refund by canceling the plan within that window. The refund is processed automatically to your original payment method and may take up to 20 business days to appear on your statement. The refund policy does not apply to plan renewals or upgrades of existing plans. If you cancel within the first 14 days, your plan is immediately deactivated. If you cancel after 14 days, the plan remains active until the end of the current billing cycle and is not refunded.

Note: In the Studio Editor, many mobile customizations are available, but you cannot select the checkout button placement there.

According to the Wix documentation, it takes time for search engines to recognize that old URLs have changed or are no longer available, and the removal process depends entirely on the individual search engine. Since you have already submitted removal requests and your updated sitemap, the documentation recommends that after sending a removal request in Google Search Console you should also request indexing for those URLs so Google re-crawls them. Make sure your site is verified with Google Search Console (Wix can do this via the Wix SEO Setup Checklist, or you can verify manually) to use the URL removal tool. Changes and removals are not instant—Google must re-crawl the pages before the old versions disappear from search results.

For an image carried over from your desktop site, open your mobile editor and click the image. Then click the Settings icon to adjust image settings (options include Reset Image Proportions and Image Behaviors for click interactions). You can also click the Crop icon to crop the image or the Animation icon to add an animation. Note: The provided documentation does not specify brightness or contrast adjustment options for images carried over from desktop; it only lists settings, crop, and animation as the available customizations for carried-over images.

To sell products on your Wix site, add Wix Stores to your site, then create your products (physical or digital) and add up to 15 images, GIFs, or videos. Connect at least one payment method (e.g., credit/debit cards, PayPal, or Wix Payments). Set up shipping and delivery options such as free shipping, flat rate, rate by weight, rate by price, local delivery, or store pickup, and configure tax rules for your region. After your store is live, manage orders by adding tracking numbers, marking orders as paid and fulfilled, and shipping them. If you prefer not to set up a full online store, you can instead add a PayPal Buy Now button to sell individual products directly through PayPal.

To temporarily remove the Quick Action Bar from your mobile site, right-click the Quick Action Bar in the mobile Editor and select Delete. Note that when you remove it, the details you entered for each action are removed as well; if you re-add the Quick Action Bar later, you will need to manually enter the relevant information again.

In the New Automation Builder, when you edit your automated email template, you can add personalized content (also called dynamic values or variables) to insert the recipient's name. These are pieces of code that display different information to each user based on their data, such as their first name. Note that personalized content does not appear in test emails, but recipients will see it when the automation is actually sent.

To create a custom sign-up form linked to your Members Area: First, ensure you have a Members Area on your site. In the Wix Editor, click Pages & Menu on the left, then click Signup & Login. Documents may be rejected for several reasons. For your photo ID: it must be a color, active (non-expired) passport, driver's license, or government ID showing all 4 borders/corners, not blurry/overexposed, not a screenshot, straightened (not angled), and your first/middle/last name and birth date in your Wix Payments account must exactly match the ID. For driver's licenses or government ID cards, send a separate file for each side; for passports with an MRZ, the MRZ must be visible. For address verification (e.g., utility bill): it must be dated within the last 6 months, show the full name and address clearly, and include at least one full page. For bank documents (statement, voided check, or bank letter): they must be issued within the last 12 months, be clear and legible (not blurry, torn, rotated, or a mobile screenshot), show the full bank account number and bank logo, and the account holder/company name must match your Wix Payments account details exactly. For company documents: the tax ID/registration number and company name must be visible and match your account, and the document must be issued within the last 12 months. All documents must be in HEIC, JPEG, JPG, PDF, or PNG format, max 10 MB (min 1 KB for PDF, 100 KB for other formats), and must be issued in the same country as your selected business location (for business accounts, your ID may be from any Wix Payments supported country). Verification can take up to 7 business days; if 7 business days have passed and you've confirmed all details match, contact Wix Customer Care.

Emails may be marked as spam or not received due to three main factors: sender reputation, sender identification (SPF/DKIM protocols), and email content. To improve deliverability: (1) Only email subscribers who have consented, and build your list organically with double opt-in—never use purchased or scraped lists. (2) Regularly maintain your list by removing inactive subscribers, non-existent addresses, and providing an easy unsubscribe option to avoid hard bounces that hurt your reputation. (3) Write clear, non-clickbait subject lines and clearly identify your business name and address in the email footer. (4) Keep content relevant and engaging to encourage opens and clicks, which boosts sender reputation. (5) Gradually increase sending volume rather than sudden spikes. (6) Note that Wix Email Marketing automatically adds DNS records (3 sendgrid.net and 2 ascendbywix.com keys) to validate campaigns when using a custom mailbox. If campaigns still aren't reaching inboxes, ask subscribers to check their spam folder, add your 'From' address to their contacts, and check webmail provider rules (delivery can take up to 24 hours). Review your sender reputation, content, and identification protocols, and consider contacting Wix support if issues persist.

To get your site indexed and appearing in search results: 1) Check if your site is indexed by searching 'site:' followed by your domain (e.g., site:yourdomain.com). 2) Ensure your site is published, as search engines only index published pages and changes. 3) Go to your SEO Dashboard > Go to SEO Settings and make sure the 'Let search engines index your site' toggle is enabled. 4) Check that specific pages aren't blocked: verify they don't have a 'noindex' robots meta tag, aren't password protected, don't have 301 redirects (delete them if they do), and reset any custom canonical tags to default. 5) Ensure pages have enough content (at least 250-400 words) to avoid soft 404 errors. 6) Add internal links between your pages to help search engines understand your site structure. 7) Use the Wix SEO Setup Checklist to optimize keywords, title tags, and meta descriptions, which also submits your site directly to Google for indexing. 8) Submit your sitemap directly to Google or submit individual page URLs if you made recent changes. 9) Make sure your content follows Google's E-E-A-T guidelines (Experience, Expertise, Authority, Trustworthiness). 10) Check for manual actions in Google Search Console. Note that it can take time for Google to crawl and index your site, and ranking high requires ongoing effort including fresh content and backlinks.

Billing for Google Ads with Wix works through a monthly subscription model combined with ad credits. Your monthly subscription is billed monthly (before VAT) as a whole for all campaigns you run. This occurs because JARs in the WAS server's plugins directory enforce an 'exports list' honored by the server's class loader. Classes in plugin JARs that are not on the exports list are treated as internal use only, so RAD (or the snippet editor) may show them as available for compilation, but at runtime a NoClassDefFoundError is thrown when user code tries to call them. To resolve, either place the JAR in the server's library directory instead of the plugins directory (a different class loader is used that does not implement the exports list), or download the required class directly from its source (e.g., Apache) and place that JAR on the server's classpath.

Locate the Obj={pool:X;obj:Y;type:Z} field in the db2diag.log corruption entry. In this notation, pool is the Tablespace ID, obj is the Object ID, and type indicates the object type (0 = Table, 1 = Index). To retrieve the object name and schema, run the following query substituting the values from the log entry: db2 "select char(tabname,20), char(tabschema,20) from syscat.tables where tableid=<ObjectID> and tbspaceid=<TablespaceID>". For example, for Obj={pool:3;obj:21;type:0}, execute: db2 "select char(tabname,20), char(tabschema,20) from syscat.tables where tableid=21 and tbspaceid=3".

The upgrade fails during the ejbdeploy step because stale OSGI cache remains for the ejbdeploy tool after the WebSphere Application Server was upgraded. The OSGI class of the ejbdeploy tool contains class information within the deploytool folder and can become stale if the content inside deploytool has changed, causing ADMA5008E (EJBDeploy program failed), ADMA0063E (error during EJB deployment), ADMA5069E (installation of application wps failed), and WASX7017E (exception received while running the script). To resolve, delete/remove the contents of the deploytool configuration directory (paths vary by WAS version, e.g., <profile root>/deploytools/configuration for WAS v6.1.x) EXCEPT for the 'config.ini' file if it exists, then retry the CF upgrade.

The documentation does not specify the exact precision (e.g., millisecond-level accuracy) of the backside persistent timeout value. However, the 'Failed to process response headers' error is not necessarily caused by timeout precision. According to the technote, this error almost always indicates a connection failure where the service received no data—typically because a reused persistent connection was already closed by the backend (or an external device) before DataPower attempted to use it, or due to a slow response causing timeout before headers arrive. Even with DataPower's timeout set lower (28s) than the backend's (30s), the error can occur if DataPower attempts to reuse a connection that the backend has already terminated. The suggested workaround is to lower the DataPower persistent timeout further or disable persistent connections entirely.

The use of the Client Channel Definition Table (CCDT) with XA connections is not supported. This restriction exists because of transaction recovery: if the application server stops while there are still active transactions, there is no way with the current implementation to ensure that it will connect to the same queue manager when it restarts, which can lead to in-doubt transactions being left dangling and never resolved. When attempting to create an XA connection using a connection factory that uses a CCDT, you will receive error MQJMS1068: failed to obtain XAResource. To resolve this, do not use the CCDT-based connection factory (jms/QM) for XA transactions; use direct connections to specific queue managers (such as jms/QM01 or jms/QM02) instead.

On a 64-bit JVM using compressed references, the Class Pointer and Monitor/Lock fields use 32-bit pointers and must be allocated in the first 4GB of the address space (the low-memory region). Even if the system has plenty of free memory overall, the OS memory allocator may exhaust the low-memory region under 4GB, causing the JVM to throw a Native OutOfMemory (NOOM) when it cannot allocate these required structures. To resolve this, you can use the -Xmcrs parameter (available in Java 6.0.16.3, 6.1.8.3, 7.0.8.10, 7.1.2.10 and later) to reserve more low memory at startup, set -Xgc:preferredHeapBase=<address> or -Xmx4G, or decrease the size and usage of application Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks.

For IBM Integration Bus (IIB) v10.0.0.9 and later, generate a Java thread dump (javacore) against an execution group using the mqsichangeproperties command: mqsichangeproperties <Int.Node> -e <Int.Server> -o ComIbmInternalSupportManager/Java/JVM -n dump -v core (or -v all to produce heapdump, javacore, and system dump). The -v core option produces a javacore (thread dump) and is available on IBM JRE platforms (all platforms except HP and Solaris). Dump files are output to $MQSI_WORKPATH/common/errors. Note that collecting Java core dumps is invasive and will impact the performance of the Integration Server process.

The Plug-in cannot locate the IBM Global Security Kit (GSKit) libraries required for SSL initialization. To resolve this, set the LD_LIBRARY_PATH environment variable to point to the GSKit library directory that comes with the Plug-in. For a 64-bit Plug-in v8.x used with a 64-bit Apache on Linux, use: export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/IBM/WebSphere/Plugins/gsk8/gsk8_64/lib64/ . Note that simply setting this from the command line before starting the web server may not work; instead, add the export command to the web server's environment file (e.g., /etc/sysconfig/httpd for RHEL or /usr/sbin/envvars for SLES/SUSE) so the variable is set when the web server starts.

This information is documented in IBM Security Bulletin swg21975233. The bulletin states that CVE-2015-7575 (the MD5 'SLOTH' vulnerability on TLS 1.2) affects WebSphere Message Broker and IBM Integration Bus versions 9.0 and 10.0 on AIX, HP-UX, Linux, Solaris, and Windows. The vulnerability allows a man-in-the-middle attacker to impersonate a TLS server and obtain credentials via a collision attack when MD5 is used to sign the ServerKeyExchange message during a TLS handshake. CVSS Base Score is 7.1. No workarounds or mitigations are listed. The bulletin was originally published on 23 Jan 2016 and reported by Karthikeyan Bhargavan at INRIA.

If you performed a binary installation and created the profile later, or migrated from 6.1.x, ensure the PortalServer/wps.properties file correctly references the primary profile by adding ProfileName=<your profile name> if it does not exist.

These are false error messages that can occur on the DataPower 9235 appliance. The problem does not affect appliance operation other than the continuous failure message. First, confirm the power supplies are working normally by checking the LED status on the power supplies - if the LEDs are green, the power supplies are working normally. To recover from the false errors, perform a reboot of the appliance. From the WebGUI: Control Panel → System Control → In the 'Shutdown' section choose 'Reboot System' then click 'Shutdown'. From the CLI: enter 'top', then 'shutdown reboot', then 'y'. This resets the sensors and in most cases no additional errors are logged. If the issue reoccurs on the same appliance, contact IBM DataPower support with information including how many times the issue occurred and outputs from CLI commands: show clock, show version, show ipmi, show sensors-other, config, service show, and test hardware.

To identify indexing errors in the Atlas database:

1. Login to the Atlas database as the PSSAPL user.
2. Run the query: select * from ctx_user_index_errors;
3. Copy the value in the ERR_TEXTKEY field from the results.
4. Run the query: select * from documentlibrary where rowid='<value from Step 3>';
5. This will list the document that has the indexing error.

Note: Sometimes encrypted and password protected documents cause document indexing errors.

The unusually small war and ear files occur because the create_web_client_war.sh script fails to change directory into the WorkplaceXT directory due to the CDPATH operating system environment variable being set. When CDPATH is set, the cd command in the script jumps to an unintended directory (such as the root of the file system) instead of the expected '<WorkplaceXT_install_directory>/IBM/FileNet/webclient/' directory, resulting in the error 'create_web_client_war.sh[5]: cd: .WorkplaceXT: [No such file or directory]'. This causes the archive to be created without the proper contents, making it only a few kilobytes and causing the WebSphere deployment error 'IWAE0006E Archive is not a valid WAR File because the deployment descriptor can not be found (case sensitive): WEB-INF/web.xml'. To resolve this, unset the CDPATH environment variable while creating the IBM FileNet Workplace XT war and ear files.

To remove the default compressed references (-Xcompressedrefs) in WebSphere Application Server on 64-bit JVMs, add -Xnocompressedrefs as a generic JVM argument. This disables compressed references and removes the 4GB memory restriction on Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks, but will significantly increase Java heap memory requirements (it is not uncommon for 70% more heap space to be required), so the Java heap size should be adjusted to a larger value and garbage collection monitored and retuned as required.

The information is available in IBM Security Bulletin swg21998655 titled 'Malicious File Download vulnerability in IBM Business Process Manager (BPM) and WebSphere Lombardi Edition (WLE) - CVE-2016-9693'. Affected products include IBM Business Process Manager Standard, IBM Business Process Manager Express, and WebSphere Lombardi Edition across versions 7.5 through 8.5.7. The fix is iFix JR57149, which disables the vulnerable URL and uses HTML5 features to trigger CSV download without server interaction. For IBM BPM V8.0.0.0 through V8.0.1.3, upgrade to minimal Refresh Pack 1, install Fix Pack 3, then apply iFix JR57149. For IBM BPM V8.5.0.0 through V8.5.0.2, install Fix Pack 2 then apply iFix JR57149. For IBM BPM V8.5.5.0, apply iFix JR57149 directly. IBM BPM V7.5 and WebSphere Lombardi Edition are out of general support; customers with support extension contracts can contact IBM support to request the fix.

When multiple versions of JDBC drivers from the same vendor (e.g., both ojdbc6.jar and ojdbc14.jar) are configured in WebSphere Application Server, irrespective of the scopes, there is a possibility of a collision of the classes and WAS cannot predict from which version of the driver jar the class will be loaded. This is why the SystemOut.log shows the older driver version (DSRA8206I) even though the JDBC provider is configured with ojdbc6.jar. To resolve this, go to the JDBC Provider configuration and enable "Isolate this resource provider". When enabled, it ensures that only the jar specified in the classpath for that particular JDBC provider will be used for all datasources under it. Also verify that WebSphere variables such as ORACLE_JDBC_DRIVER_PATH or VMM_JDBC_CLASSPATH (stored in variables.xml at cell or node scope) are not referencing the older ojdbc14.jar.

By default, Solaris does not write verbose GC output to a log file; it must be explicitly configured. To write verbose GC output to a file other than native_stdout on Solaris (SunOS), add the following parameters to the generic JVM arguments: -XX:+PrintGCDetails, -XX:+PrintGCDateStamps, -XX:+PrintHeapAtGC, and -Xloggc:/tmp/gc.log (replace /tmp/gc.log with your desired file path). To enable log file rotation, additionally add: -XX:+UseGCLogFileRotation, -XX:NumberOfGCLogFiles=10, and -XX:GCLogFileSize=10M. Note that -Xloggc:<fileName> specifies the log file path, and rotation requires -Xloggc to be set.

The behavior is controlled by the transaction timeout, not the session timeout. In ODM TeamServer (RTS/DC), the property ilog.rules.teamserver.transaction.timeout in the teamserver web module's WEB-INF/web.xml controls this (default 600 seconds / 10 minutes). If a transactional operation takes longer than this, the transaction is rolled back and the user is effectively kicked out of the operation. Additionally, application server container-level transaction timeouts (e.g., WebSphere 'Maximum transaction timeout') can also trigger this and should be checked and increased if needed.

Beginning with firmware version 6.0 and above, the default SSL settings changed: Crypto profiles now enable TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.1 by default. When DataPower acts as the SSL client, this changes the protocol version included in the Client Hello. Some legacy servers with non-compliant SSL implementations reject connection attempts when TLSv1.2 or TLSv1.1 are used, causing the handshake to fail without negotiating to a mutually agreeable protocol. To resolve, upgrade the SSL server to a compliant version, or if required, disable TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.1 within the Crypto Profile (Objects > Crypto Configuration > Crypto Profile) to allow compatibility.

In a clustered environment, the most likely causes for the latest ruleset not executing after a 'Replace RuleApp Version' deployment are: (1) the hot deployment notification was not sent by the RES console or not received by all Execution Units (XU) in the cluster, often due to insufficient administrative rights (Monitor role in WebSphere Application Server) for the publishing user to notify all Execution Units through JMX; (2) asynchronous ruleset parsing is enabled, causing executions to temporarily use an earlier version while the updated ruleset is being parsed; or (3) the updated ruleset cannot be parsed successfully, causing RES to fall back on an earlier active version that parses. Validate that the hot deployment completed successfully across all cluster nodes and check the ruleset parsing policy settings.

The error is caused by the Windows security policy 'System Cryptography: Use FIPS compliant algorithms for encryption, hashing and signing' being enabled, which prevents the FIPS key from being encrypted/decrypted during key import. To resolve: 1) Open Local Security Policy under Administrative Tools, 2) Navigate to Local Policies > Security Options, 3) Set 'System Cryptography: Use FIPS compliant algorithms for encryption, hashing and signing' to Disabled, then retry the key import. Additionally, verify that encryption has been fully set up on the server and that the dc_ktf.xml key file has been properly distributed/imported to the client folder; if this is a new server where Datacap has never run, the encryption keys must first be exported on the server before clients can import them.

The 'Too many open files' error indicates the Portal server process has exhausted its file handle limit (which includes sockets), typically caused by system configuration limits (ulimit set too low) or file descriptor leaks in the application. To resolve: 1) Check current limits using `ulimit -Sn` (soft limit) and `ulimit -Hn` (hard limit), or capture a javacore with `kill -3 PID` to view the NOFILE limit. 2) Increase the file descriptor limit using `ulimit -n [value]` (a value of 8000 is usually sufficient for normal runtime), but note these settings only take effect after restarting the application server and nodeagent on the same command line where the ulimit was executed. 3) If the error persists even with a high limit, check for file descriptor leaks by monitoring open files over time using `lsof -p [PID] -r [interval in seconds]` (e.g., 1800 for 30 minutes) on AIX/Linux, or `procfiles -n [PID]`, to identify if the number of open files/sockets is growing continuously.

Yes, by default when an SCA module is uninstalled (or updated), its associated destinations are removed even if messages still reside on them, which would result in message loss. To prevent this, set the custom JVM property SCA.recycleDestinations to false for the module; this preserves the SCA destinations and their messages during module updates. While monitoring internal queues (sca/<module>/... on the SCA.SYSTEM bus) to ensure they are empty before updating is a valid precaution, the documented method to preserve messages is to configure SCA.recycleDestinations=false, particularly important when Event Sequencing is used.

The HTTP Session time-out for a Workplace application on WebSphere Application Server can be set in the following locations, listed from lowest to highest precedence:

1. **Server Level** (Administrative Console): Navigate to Servers > Application Servers > Your Server > Web Container > Session Management. This is the lowest precedence level.

2. **Enterprise Application Level** (Administrative Console): Navigate to Applications > Enterprise Applications > Your Application > Session Management. Check 'Override' in the Override Session Management section to override the Server Level setting.

3. **Web Application Level** (Administrative Console): Navigate to Applications > Enterprise Applications > Your Application > Web Module > Your Web App.war > Session Management. Check 'Override' to override both Server and Enterprise Application settings.

4. **Application Packaging (web.xml)**: Set during application packaging in the web.xml file using <session-config><session-timeout>value</session-timeout></session-config> (value in minutes). This overrides all Administrative Console settings.

5. **Application Code**: Set programmatically by invoking setMaxInactiveInterval() on the HttpSession object. This has the highest precedence and overrides all other settings.

To increase the time-out, modify the appropriate level based on your requirements, keeping in mind that higher precedence settings (web.xml and application code) will override lower ones.

Theme resources are cached by the browser/proxy using a digest in the URL. The resolver uses this digest to cache URLs like resource aggregator collections, and the digest remains the same between restarts, causing the browser to serve cached files (HTTP 304) instead of loading updated resources from the server. To force the updated theme resources to load, set the 'digest.seed' key in the WP ConfigService to any string value. This generates a new digest on server boot, changing the URLs and forcing the browser to fetch the updated files.

This is a known DB2 11 for z/OS defect documented in APAR PI19804. SQLCODE -401 (DSNT408I) with SQLERRP=DSNXOBFC occurs during CREATE PROCEDURE for a native SQL procedure (or compiled SQL scalar function) when a control statement contains an IN-LIST predicate that references SQL variables (e.g., IF var IN (sqlvar1, sqlvar2)). DB2 11 does not process the SQL variables in the IN-LIST predicate correctly, causing the 'operands not comparable' error. The CIUSNTSR stored procedure created by CICS IA CIUDBCQ JCL contains such a construct. Apply PTF UI20622 (the fix for PI19804) to resolve the issue.
